# Description

```{r Libraries, message=FALSE}
library(stringr)
library(dplyr)

library(rols)
```

# gnomAD data download
All these steps were performed on hpc orthus. It downloads a lot of data but the final file is about 240 MB big. Each step was ran with shell scripts. The scripts use bcftools lib which can be ran with a singularity container (orthus) or installed locally.

## 1-download_merge.sh
Downloading the whole clinvar db and gnomad data by chromosome. Merging (joining) data from clinvar to gnomad varinats by chromosome.
```{}
if [ ! -f "clinvar_20220205.vcf.gz" ]; then
  echo "Downloading ClinVar data"
  wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/clinvar/vcf_GRCh37/clinvar_20220205.vcf.gz
  tabix clinvar_20220205.vcf.gz
fi

for chr in {{1..22},X,Y};
  do
  gdir="chr${chr}"
  
  if [ ! -f ${gdir} ]; then
    mkdir ${gdir}
  fi
  
  filename="gnomad.exomes.r2.1.1.sites.${chr}.vcf.bgz"
  echo "Processing chromosome ${chr}"
  cd ${gdir}
  if [ ! -f ${filename} ]; then
    wget https://storage.googleapis.com/gcp-public-data--gnomad/release/2.1.1/vcf/exomes/${filename}
  fi    
  tabix -p vcf ${filename}
  bcftools isec -c none -p dir ${filename} ../clinvar_20220205.vcf.gz
  cd dir
  bgzip 0002.vcf
  tabix 0002.vcf.gz   
  bgzip 0003.vcf
  tabix 0003.vcf.gz
  
  bcftools merge --merge all 0002.vcf.gz 0003.vcf.gz > ../merged_${chr}.vcf
  
  
  cd ../..
  done
```

## 2-concat.sh
Concatinating all chromosomes into one.
```{}
bcftools concat -o gnomad_all.vcf chr1/merged_1.vcf chr2/merged_2.vcf chr3/merged_3.vcf chr4/merged_4.vcf chr5/merged_5.vcf chr6/merged_6.vcf chr7/merged_7.vcf chr8/merged_8.vcf chr9/merged_9.vcf chr10/merged_10.vcf chr11/merged_11.vcf chr12/merged_12.vcf chr13/merged_13.vcf chr14/merged_14.vcf chr15/merged_15.vcf chr16/merged_16.vcf chr17/merged_17.vcf chr18/merged_18.vcf chr19/merged_19.vcf chr20/merged_20.vcf chr21/merged_21.vcf chr22/merged_22.vcf chrY/merged_Y.vcf chrX/merged_X.vcf
```

## 3-removing_annotations.sh
The joined gnomad clinvar vcf contains around 1000 annotation information. This script removes all annotations exepct the ones listed in the command. Basic info is containt, some info from gnomad and all clinvar. !!!
```{}
bcftools annotate -x ^INFO/AC,^INFO/AN,^INFO/AF,^INFO/AF_ESP,^INFO/AF_EXAC,^INFO/AF_TGP,^INFO/ALLELEID,^INFO/CLNDN,^INFO/CLNDNINCL,^INFO/CLNDISDB,^INFO/CLNDISDBINCL,^INFO/CLNHGVS,^INFO/CLNREVSTAT,^INFO/CLNSIG,^INFO/CLNSIGCONF,^INFO/CLNSIGINCL,^INFO/CLNVC,^INFO/CLNVCSO,^INFO/CLNVI,^INFO/DBVARID,^INFO/GENEINFO gnomad_clinvar_genome.vcf > gnomad.vcf
```

Some usefull commands
```{}
# extracting headers
grep "##" data > header_vcf.txt

# extracting first 10000 lines
head -n 2000 data > test1k_data.vcf
```

# VCF:Loading data
Next we load the gnomad.vcf and converting the vcf format to a data frame.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
gnomad_vcf <- read.vcfR("codingVariants/data/gnomad.vcf")

# This call takes a long time
vcf_df <- cbind(as.data.frame(getFIX(gnomad_vcf)), INFO2df(gnomad_vcf))

vcf_df$clinvarID <- str_split(vcf_df$ID, pattern = ";", simplify = TRUE)[,2]
vcf_df$ID <- str_split(vcf_df$ID, pattern = ";", simplify = TRUE)[,1]
vcf_df$gene <- str_split(vcf_df$GENEINFO, pattern = ":", simplify = TRUE)[,1]

saveRDS(vcf_df, "codingVariants/RDS/gnomad_clinvar_df_raw.rds")
rm(vcf_df)
rm(gnomad_vcf)
```
### clnv data cleanup

1) Removing non informative columns
   AC, AN, DBVARID - only NA
   suffix INCL - info about the alternative allele
   AF_ESP, AF_EXAC, AF_TGP, - high % of NA (50%)
   CLNVCSO - Sequence ontology
   QUAL - Phred quality score.Vals are above 30- base call accuracy 99,9%
   CLNVI
   
2) Filtering rows
   CLNDN - Disease name that contain NA, not_provided, not_specified
   FILTER - Selecting only those that pass the filter to reduce for reducing FP
    

```{r}
clnv <- readRDS("RDS/gnomad_clinvar_df_raw.rds") %>%
  # This filter reduces number of rows for 200k 
  dplyr::filter(FILTER == "PASS" & !is.element(CLNDN, c(NA,"not_provided","not_specified", "not_specified|not_provided","	
not_specified|not_provided"))) %>%
  # Removing non informative cols
  select(-c(AC, AN, DBVARID, CLNDISDBINCL, CLNSIGINCL, AF_ESP, AF_EXAC, AF_TGP, CLNVCSO, QUAL, FILTER, CLNVI)) %>%
  # Using a tidyr function that separates pipe sep vals into rows 
  separate_rows(CLNDN, CLNDISDB, sep = "\\|") %>%
  # Lower casing the whole name
  mutate(CLNDN = tolower(CLNDN)) %>%
  # Removing rows with unknown pheontypes, disease names
  dplyr::filter(!is.element(CLNDN,c("not_specified","not_provided")) & CLNDISDB != ".")
```


```{r, eval=FALSE}
saveRDS(clnv, file="codingVariants/RDS/gnomad_clinvar_df_clean.rds")
write.table(clnv, file = "codingVariants/output/clinVar.xlsx")
```


# Ontolgy:Loading
Loading working objects:
efo_mappings whcih contains pairs of efo_ids and corresponding cross-ref. 
efo_terms which is a list of Terms - object from the rols library. It contains all efo ids.
clnv is the object which stores coding SNPs from gnomad with matching clinvar disease annotations.
```{r}
# Dataframe of paired efo_id and crossrefrence with labels
efo_mappings <- readRDS("RDS/efo_mappings.rds")
# list of Terms (rols object)
efo_terms <- readRDS("RDS/efo_terms.rds")
# Snps deposited in gnomad and annotated in clinvar
clnv <- readRDS("RDS/gnomad_clinvar_df_clean.rds")
```

## Preprocessing clinvar terms
Clinvar disease ids (CLNDISDB) are stored in one column. Cross refed ids are comma separated and are not standardized (eg. MONDO:MONDO:..):
MONDO:MONDO:0014052,MedGen:C3808739,OMIM:615120

```{r}
clnv_terms <-
  clnv%>%
  select(CLNDISDB, CLNDN) %>%
  unique() %>%
  # Separatig rows by ontology ids, disease names are contained
  separate_rows(CLNDISDB, sep =",")

clnv_terms$CLN_diseaseID <- NA

# Removing the front part of some ids eg EFO:EFO_0000275
# Some have multiple parts so looping is an easier way to go
for(i in 1:length(clnv_terms$CLNDISDB)){
    if(str_detect(clnv_terms$CLNDISDB[i], pattern = "EFO")){
    clnv_terms$CLNDISDB[i] <- sub("_",":",clnv_terms$CLNDISDB[i])
  }
  
  num <- str_count(clnv_terms$CLNDISDB[i],pattern = ":")

  clnv_terms$CLN_diseaseID[i] <-
    str_split(clnv_terms$CLNDISDB[i], pattern = ":", simplify = TRUE)[,c(num,num+1)] %>%
    paste(collapse = ":")
}

```

## Adding mondo id col to clinvar data
```{r}
clnv <-
  clnv %>%
  left_join( select(filter(clnv_terms, str_detect(CLN_diseaseID, pattern="MONDO")),
                    CLNDN,
                    MONDO_ID = CLN_diseaseID)) %>%
  mutate(gene = str_split(GENEINFO, pattern = ":", simplify = TRUE)[,1])

# these do not have MONDO ID's, figure what to do with them  
filter(clnv, is.na(MONDO_ID))

  clnv %>%
  left_join( clnv_terms, by = "CLNDN") %>%
  mutate(gene = str_split(GENEINFO, pattern = ":", simplify = TRUE)[,1])

```

# Combining GRB data
We add affected gene info that is associated with a disease.

## GWAS:Loading
```{r}
loci_in_GRBs <- read.csv("data/loci_in_GRBs.df.csv")
```

Adding MONDO ids in a separate column in gwas_grb dataset.
1. Adding cross refed MONDO ids that are stored in efo_mappings id2
2. Adding MONDO ids that are part of EFO and are stored in efo_mappings id1
```{r}
loci_in_GRBs <-
  loci_in_GRBs %>%
  # Adding MONDO cross-ref ids into a column
  left_join(filter(efo_mappings, str_detect(id2, "MONDO")), 
            by= c("MAPPED_TRAIT_ID" = "id1")) %>%
  # Removing label since its duplicated
  select(-label)

# Changing the colname to something appropriate
names(loci_in_GRBs)[names(loci_in_GRBs)=="id2"] <- "MONDO_ID"

loci_in_GRBs <-
  loci_in_GRBs %>%
  # Copying MONDO ids from EFO
  mutate(MONDO_ID = ifelse(is.na(MONDO_ID) & str_detect(MAPPED_TRAIT_ID, "MONDO"), MAPPED_TRAIT_ID, MONDO_ID))

```

### Exploration
```{r, eval=FALSE}
View(as.data.frame(table(filter(gwas_grb, is.na(id2))$MAPPED_TRAIT)))


filter(gwas_grb, !is.na(id2))
```

## Clinvar genes to gwas
First storing disease - gene association into a separate dataframe also concatinating genes to a single row per disease.
This is the main information acquired from clinvar
```{r}
# clinvar disease gene associations
clnv_disease_gene <- 
  clnv %>%
  select(MONDO_ID, gene) %>%
  unique() %>%
  group_by(MONDO_ID) %>%
  summarise(clnv_gene = toString(gene)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(MONDO_ID))

gwas_grb_clnv <- 
  left_join(loci_in_GRBs, clnv_disease_gene)
```


```{r}
filter(gwas_grb_clnv, !is.na(clnv_gene)) %>%
  select(MAPPED_TRAIT, GWAS_GENES, GRB_GENES, clnv_gene) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  View()
```
